title: Deployment network proof of compliance runbook
body:
Purpose:
This runbook describes a reproducible 'proof-of-compliance' workflow for Private deployments that bundles network hardening artifacts: VPC topology assertions, firewall rule snapshots, mTLS service-to-service evidence, RBAC v2 bindings, and SIEM-ready audit exports. Goal: create a single, verifiable evidence bundle that satisfies security reviews and audit requests with minimal manual steps.

Scope:
- Applies to Private deployments (VPC, VPC-peered, and on-prem equivalent) for production and staging clusters.
- Focus: network controls + telemetry needed by Compliance (SOC/ISO) reviews, CFEs, and sales security questionnaires.
- Out of scope: application-layer data retention policies and encryption-at-rest (see other runbooks).

High-level flow (single-pass):
1) Snapshot network topology (subnets, route tables, NACLs).
2) Export firewall rule set (per-cluster and per-subnet).
3) Capture mTLS mesh config & cert fingerprints (active services).
4) Pull RBAC v2 role bindings and policy assertions for control plane and operator identities.
5) Export audit log schema rows and push to SIEM staging bucket.
6) Run evidence validation tests and assemble evidence manifest (signed).
7) Push artifact to retention store and update ticket/Confluence.

Quick ASCII diagram (logical):
  On-prem/VPC Customer
  +------------------------------+
  |            VPC               |
  |  +------+    +----------+    |
  |  | SubA |--->| NAT GW   |    |
  |  +------+    +----------+    |
  |     |            |           |
  |  +---------------------+     |
  |  | Private Subnet (pods) |    |
  |  +---------------------+     |
  |     | mTLS service mesh         |
  +------------------------------+
          |        |         |
       SIEM    Evidence    Control Plane
       Forward  Collector   (RBAC/audit)

NOTE: Diagram is conceptual; include AWS/GCP/Azure specifics in snapshots below.

RBAC v2 mapping (example assertions to collect):
- control-plane-admins -> groups: infra-ops, security-oncall
- egress-proxy-runner -> role: network-proxy, allowed: tcp:0-65535->10.0.0.0/16:443 (only outbound to specific endpoints)
- model-serving-ops -> role: deploy, allowed actions: deploy:create, config:update, kv:get

For each cluster, run: (example commands)
- rbac export: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://control-plane.internal/api/v2/rbac/export > rbac-v2-$(date +%F).ndjson
- minimal verify: ./tools/rbac-assert --input rbac-v2-2025-02-20.ndjson --expect control-plane-admins=infra-ops

Audit log schema (recommended canonical fields):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- request_id (uuid)
- principal (subject id: user/service account)
- principal_type (human|service|external)
- action (string e.g., route.create, model.invoke)
- resource (ARN-like or path)
- outcome (success|failure|denied)
- source_ip
- user_agent
- proto (http/grpc)
- latency_ms
- metadata (flat JSON string) -- keep small, parsed by SIEM parser

SIEM export pipeline (recommended):
1) Control plane and runtime export: daily ndjson files to secure S3/GCS bucket with object lifecycle (30d hot, 365d cold).
2) SIEM forwarder (lambda/k8s sidecar) picks up new objects, transforms to vendor format (CEF/Elastic ECS), adds tenant tags, and posts to SIEM ingestion endpoint.
3) Verify hashes and retention after ingestion.

Example ECS mapping snippet (flat):
- event.created (timestamp) <- timestamp
- host.ip (source) <- source_ip
- user.name <- principal
- event.action <- action
- event.outcome <- outcome
- network.transport <- proto
- detection.tags <- [rbac-v2,private-deploy]

Firewall rule snapshot template (capture exact fields):
- rule_id: string
- scope: VPC|subnet|instance
- direction: ingress|egress
- protocol: tcp|udp|icmp|all
- ports: single|range
- cidr: source/destination
- description: free text
- enabled: true|false
- created_by: principal
- last_modified: iso-date

Canonical firewall verification commands (examples):
- aws cli: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC_ID --output json > fw-sg-$VPC_ID.json
- gcp: gcloud compute firewall-rules list --filter="network:projects/$PROJECT/global/networks/$NETWORK" --format=json > fw-$NETWORK.json

mTLS evidence collection checklist:
- Extract current mesh control plane configuration (istio/consul/linkerd).
- For each service, record: service name, namespace, cert fingerprint (SHA256), cert issuer, expiry date, TLS version policy.
- Verify enforcement mode (STRICT/PERMISSIVE) for pod-to-pod and ingress.
- Collect kube-apiserver client CA bundles used for service account tokens if applicable.
- Commands: kubectl -n $NS get configmap mesh-certs -o yaml > mesh-certs-$NS.yaml; openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 -in cert.pem

Sample cert evidence line (manifest-friendly, TSV):
service	namespace	fingerprint	issuer	expires	enforcement_mode
model-host	inference	C2:3F:...:9A	Internal-CA	2025-10-01	STRICT

Evidence automation outline (scripts and verification):
1) collector/scan-network.sh --vpc $VPC --out /tmp/evidence/$ID/ (produces fw.json, routes.json, subnet-table.json)
2) collector/collect-mtls.sh --kubeconfig $KUBECONFIG --out /tmp/evidence/$ID/ (produces mesh-certs-*.yaml, cert-manifest.tsv)
3) collector/export-rbac.sh --token $TOKEN --out /tmp/evidence/$ID/rbac.ndjson
4) collector/export-audit.sh --since 24h --out /tmp/evidence/$ID/audit.ndjson
5) verifier/validate-evidence.py --dir /tmp/evidence/$ID --rules examples/poa-rules.yaml
6) signer/sign-manifest.sh /tmp/evidence/$ID/manifest.json > /tmp/evidence/$ID/manifest.sig

Verification tests (automated):
- Hash check: sha256sum of every artifact must match manifest and manifest.sig must be verifiable by security key.
- RBAC assertions: at least one admin group must map to infra-ops or security-oncall.
- mTLS: no service should be using plaintext ports in production subnets (script fails if found).
- Firewall: no permissive 0.0.0.0/0 inbound rules on private subnets for ports 22/443 except explicitly documented bastion/ingress.

Retention & storage recommendations:
- Evidence store: encrypted S3/GCS bucket with object-level CMAK/KMS policy, read-access only to security and audit roles.
- Hot retention: 30 days; cold archive: 3 years (or per-customer contractual requirements).
- Indexing: maintain a small searchable index (Elasticsearch/Opensearch) with pointers to artifacts and manifest checksums.

Operational playbook (common runs):
- Weekly: quick snapshot (topology+fw+rbac) automated.
- Monthly: full proof-of-compliance run (all artifacts + signer).
- Pre-release: ad-hoc run before major private-deploy customer onboarding.
- Incident: run collector with --since $(incident_start) and attach artifacts to incident ticket.

Escalation and approvals:
- If verification fails: auto-open PD-SEC ticket and notify security-oncall and infra-sre.
- Any cert expiry < 30 days triggers immediate rotation run and CAB notification.

Checklist (short):
- [ ] Topology snapshot exported
- [ ] Firewall rules snapshot completed
- [ ] mTLS cert manifest generated and validated
- [ ] RBAC v2 export exists and checks passed
- [ ] Audit logs pushed to SIEM staging bucket
- [ ] Evidence manifest signed and uploaded
- [ ] Ticket/Confluence updated with artifact links

Appendix A: Example evidence manifest fields (flat key:value entries in manifest.json):
- manifest_id: timestamp-uuid
- vpc_id: vpc-1234abcd
- artifacts: list of filenames (in index store)
- signer: infra-sre@redwood.com
- signature: base64
- validation_summary: PASSED|FAILED

Appendix B: Useful queries (SIEM)
- Find denied RBAC events: event.action:* and event.outcome:denied and tags:rbac-v2
- List services with recent cert expiry: detection.tags:mtls and event.action:cert.rotate and event.created:[now-30d TO now]

Notes and open questions (work-in-progress):
- Decide canonical retention policy per-customer (30/365/3650) to reflect contractual SLAs.
- Integrate with centralized signing service (HSM-backed) for manifest.sig rather than local key.
- Add cross-tenant correlation rules for SIEM to detect lateral movement patterns.

Contact: Marina Alvarez (mmalvarez@redwood.ai) — maintain runbook and automation scripts in infra collector repo.

End of runbook.
